SAFETY DATA SHEET COMPENDIUM -- LABORATORY REAGENTS, REV 2

This compendium summarizes hazard and physical property data for five reagents held in the general chemistry stockroom: Sulfuric Acid, Acetone, Toluene, Methanol, and Sodium Hydroxide Solution. Data below are drawn from supplier certificates of analysis and are not a substitute for the full safety data sheet.

Sulfuric Acid is a dense, corrosive liquid supplied at 98% concentration by weight. The CAS number of Sulfuric Acid is 7664-93-9. The molecular formula of Sulfuric Acid is H2SO4. The boiling point of Sulfuric Acid is 337 °C at atmospheric pressure. The occupational exposure limit for Sulfuric Acid is 1 mg/m3 as an 8-hour time-weighted average.

Acetone is a volatile, flammable solvent with the molecular formula C3H6O, used for glassware rinsing. The CAS number of Acetone is 67-64-1. The flash point of Acetone is -20 °C, well below room temperature. The vapour pressure of Acetone at 20 °C is 185 mmHg. The vapour pressure of Acetone at 25 °C is 231 mmHg.

Toluene is a clear aromatic solvent with the molecular formula C7H8, stored in the flammables cabinet. The CAS number of Toluene is 108-88-3. The occupational exposure limit for Toluene is 50 ppm as an 8-hour time-weighted average.

Methanol is a toxic, flammable alcohol with the molecular formula CH4O, used as a chromatography mobile phase. The CAS number of Methanol is 67-56-1. The boiling point of Methanol is 64.7 °C. The oral LD50 of Methanol in rats is 5628 mg/kg.

Sodium Hydroxide Solution is a caustic aqueous preparation supplied at 50% concentration by weight. The CAS number of Sodium Hydroxide Solution is 1310-73-2. A 50% aqueous solution of Sodium Hydroxide has a pH of 14. A standard solution of Sodium Hydroxide is prepared at 0.1 M for titration use.

All concentrations above are expressed by weight unless stated otherwise. Vapour pressures are reported at the stated reference temperature only and should not be extrapolated to other conditions. None of the numeric identifiers in this compendium, including CAS registry numbers and molecular formula subscripts, should be combined arithmetically with the physical property values reported alongside them.
